title: Network path was not found
message: A network-related or instance-specific error occurred. (provider: Named Pipes Provider, error: 40)
meaning: The instance was never reached. Name resolution, port, firewall or the Browser service.

title: Incorrect syntax near
message: Incorrect syntax near 'X'.
meaning: Often a compatibility level or version issue rather than a real typo, when the same code works elsewhere.

title: Incorrect syntax near a keyword
message: Incorrect syntax near the keyword 'X'.
meaning: A reserved word used as an identifier is the usual cause, and it is a different error from 102: 156 names the keyword it tripped on.

title: Invalid column name
message: Invalid column name 'X'.
meaning: Typo, wrong alias, or a column that exists in a different environment to the one you are on.

title: Invalid object name
message: Invalid object name 'dbo.X'.
meaning: Wrong database context or schema more often than a missing object.

title: Column name or number of supplied values does not match
message: Column name or number of supplied values does not match table definition.
meaning: The shape of the insert does not match the table. The static form fails at compile time, so TRY/CATCH does not catch it, and naming the columns does not help INSERT ... EXEC.

title: SELECT permission denied
message: The SELECT permission was denied on the object 'X', database 'Y', schema 'dbo'.
meaning: Object-level permission, or a DENY inherited from a role.

title: Conversion failed when converting
message: Conversion failed when converting the varchar value 'abc' to data type int.
meaning: Implicit conversion meeting a value that will not convert. Also a performance smell.

title: CREATE DATABASE permission denied
message: CREATE DATABASE permission denied in database 'master'.
meaning: Needs dbcreator or sysadmin, and it is the same shape for most CREATE permissions.

title: VIEW SERVER STATE permission denied
message: VIEW SERVER STATE permission was denied on object 'server', database 'master'.
meaning: Every interesting DMV is behind this. Database roles cannot reach it.

title: Cannot resolve the collation conflict
message: Cannot resolve the collation conflict between 'X' and 'Y' in the equal to operation.
meaning: Two sides of a comparison carry different collations. It surfaces when a query joins or compares across databases, or against tempdb, and the fix is COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT on the comparison rather than changing a column.

title: Cannot insert the value NULL into column
message: Cannot insert the value NULL into column 'X', table 'Y'; column does not allow nulls. INSERT fails.
meaning: Leaving a NOT NULL column out of the insert gives the same message as passing NULL, so check your column list before hunting for NULLs. A default rescues the omitted case but not an explicit NULL.

title: Conflict with a FOREIGN KEY constraint
message: The INSERT statement conflicted with the FOREIGN KEY constraint 'FK_X'.
meaning: The parent row does not exist, or you are deleting one that still has children.

title: Could not continue scan with NOLOCK due to data movement
message: Could not continue scan with NOLOCK due to data movement.
meaning: The cost of NOLOCK, made visible. A read can miss rows, return one twice, or fail outright like this when pages move underneath it mid-scan.

title: Attempt to fetch logical page belongs to a different object
message: Attempt to fetch logical page ... in database ... belongs to object ..., not to object ...
meaning: Allocation corruption. Stop and go to backups.

title: The filegroup has no files assigned to it
message: The filegroup "X" has no files assigned to it. Tables, indexes, text columns, ntext columns, and image columns cannot be populated on this filegroup until a file is added.
meaning: The filegroup was created and no file was ever added. CREATE TABLE on it succeeds, so the failure lands later, at the first insert.

title: Insufficient system memory
message: There is insufficient system memory in resource pool 'default' to run this query.
meaning: Real memory pressure, or a single query asking for far more than it should.

title: Insufficient memory in the buffer pool
message: There is insufficient memory available in the buffer pool.
meaning: Rarely arrives alone. In job history it is the opening line of a cascade with 9001, 3314 and 3908 behind it, and the cascade is the story rather than this row.

title: I/O error, the operating system reported a failure
message: The operating system returned error 21 to SQL Server during a read at offset 0x... in file 'X'.
meaning: The storage layer failed the request. This is hardware or driver, not SQL Server.

title: Logical consistency-based I/O error
message: SQL Server detected a logical consistency-based I/O error: incorrect checksum.
meaning: The read succeeded and the page was wrong. Check the backups before anything else.

title: Read-retry succeeded
message: A read of the file 'X' at offset ... succeeded after failing N attempt(s).
meaning: The quiet one. Severity 10 so nothing alerts, and it is the warning before 823 and 824.

title: Buffer latch timeout
message: Time-out occurred while waiting for buffer latch type X for page P, database ID N.
meaning: A page took longer than the latch would wait, which points at storage or memory pressure rather than at the query holding it.

title: Not able to access the database under the current security context
message: The server principal "X" is not able to access the database "Y" under the current security context.
meaning: Common in SSMS Object Explorer when a login has no user in one database on the instance.

title: Database is in single-user mode and already taken
message: Database 'X' is already open and can only have one user at a time.
meaning: Single user mode let one session in and it was not yours. Every other connection, including a new query window, gets this until the holder disconnects or the database goes MULTI_USER.

title: Database is in the middle of a restore
message: Database 'X' cannot be opened. It is in the middle of a restore.
meaning: RESTORING state. The question is whether a restore is running or the database was stranded.

title: Database cannot be opened because it is offline
message: Database 'X' cannot be opened because it is offline.
meaning: Nobody gets in at all, including you, until SET ONLINE. Connections are refused outright rather than queued.

title: Database cannot be opened due to inaccessible files
message: Database 'X' cannot be opened due to inaccessible files or insufficient memory or disk space.
meaning: The files are missing, the service account lost access, or the volume is gone.

title: AG database not accessible for queries
message: The target database, 'X', is participating in an availability group and is currently not accessible for queries.
meaning: A readable-secondary problem, not a restore one. The database shows ONLINE while data movement is suspended or the replica is not enabled for read access.

title: Could not allocate space, filegroup is full
message: Could not allocate space for object 'X' in database 'Y' because the 'PRIMARY' filegroup is full.
meaning: Data file, not log. Autogrowth off, disk full, or a size cap reached.

title: Deadlock victim
message: Transaction (Process ID 52) was deadlocked on lock resources with another process and has been chosen as the deadlock victim.
meaning: The engine picked the cheaper transaction to kill. The fix is in the access pattern, not the error.

title: Lock request time out period exceeded
message: Lock request time out period exceeded.
meaning: Blocking, not deadlock. Something held a lock longer than the timeout allowed.

title: CREATE DATABASE failed, files could not be created
message: CREATE DATABASE failed. Some file names listed could not be created. Check related errors.
meaning: The wrapper error, and it says so: the cause is in the errors around it. On an attach it arrives with 5120 underneath, and TRY/CATCH only ever sees this one.

title: SET options have incorrect settings
message: INSERT failed because the following SET options have incorrect settings: 'QUOTED_IDENTIFIER'. Verify that SET options are correct for use with indexed views and/or indexes on computed columns and/or filtered indexes.
meaning: The connection writing to a table with a filtered index or indexed view has the wrong SET options. Reads still work, which is why it usually shows up as one failing job. SSMS sets QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON and sqlcmd does not.

title: Cannot insert duplicate key row in unique index
message: Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'dbo.X' with unique index 'IX_Y'.
meaning: Same as 2627 but from a unique index rather than a primary key.

title: Violation of PRIMARY KEY constraint
message: Violation of PRIMARY KEY constraint 'PK_X'. Cannot insert duplicate key in object 'dbo.Y'.
meaning: A duplicate insert, often a retry that succeeded the first time.

title: String or binary data would be truncated in table
message: String or binary data would be truncated in table 'db.dbo.T', column 'c'. Truncated value: 'X'.
meaning: The 2019 and later version of 8152. It names the table, the column and the value.

title: Restore database is terminating abnormally
message: RESTORE DATABASE is terminating abnormally.
meaning: The companion message, never the cause. The error immediately above it is the real one.

title: Cannot restore, the database is in use by this session
message: RESTORE cannot process database 'X' because it is in use by this session. It is recommended that the master database be used when performing this operation.
meaning: Nothing is wrong with the backup or the target. You are connected to the database you are restoring over. Switch the session to master and run it again.

title: Striped backup, not every member was provided
message: The media set has 2 media families but only 1 are provided. All members must be provided.
meaning: The backup is striped across several files and you listed only some of them. Name every file in the set. The opposite mistake gives 3231.

title: The backup set holds a backup of a database other than the existing one
message: The backup set holds a backup of a database other than the existing 'X' database.
meaning: Restoring over a different database needs WITH REPLACE, and deserves a pause first.

title: File cannot be restored to that path
message: File 'X' cannot be restored to 'Y'. Use WITH MOVE to identify a valid location for the file.
meaning: Usually arrives right after 3634. The target folder does not exist, or the service account cannot write there. Nothing is wrong with the backup.

title: Cannot open backup device
message: Cannot open backup device 'X'. Operating system error 5(Access is denied.).
meaning: Almost always the SQL Server service account, not your own account, lacking access to the path.

title: Separate backups listed as one media set
message: The media loaded on "X" is formatted to support 1 media families, but 2 media families are expected according to the backup device specification.
meaning: The files you listed are separate backups, not members of one stripe. The opposite mistake to 3132.

title: Logical file is not part of the database
message: Logical file 'X' is not part of database 'Y'. Use RESTORE FILELISTONLY to list the logical file names.
meaning: WITH MOVE named a logical file the backup does not contain. Read the names out of the backup with RESTORE FILELISTONLY rather than assuming them from the target.

title: Media family on device is incorrectly formed
message: The media family on device 'X' is incorrectly formed. SQL Server cannot process this media family.
meaning: Wrong file, truncated copy, or a backup from a newer version being restored to an older one.

title: The backup file is truncated
message: The file ID 1 on device 'X' is incorrectly formed and can not be read.
meaning: The copy did not finish. Different from 3241, which means the file is not a backup at all; this one names the file ID it could not read.

title: Error during undo of a logged operation
message: During undoing of a logged operation in database 'X', an error occurred at log record ID N.
meaning: Severity 21. The engine could not roll something back, and the real failure is usually logged just before it. Restore or repair, do not retry.

title: Cannot recover the master database
message: Cannot recover the master database. SQL Server is unable to run.
meaning: The instance will not start. Master is damaged, moved, or its permissions changed.

title: The operating system refused the restore target
message: The operating system returned the error 'X' while attempting 'Y' on 'Z'.
meaning: The OS refused the path, and 3156 normally follows it. The folder is missing or the service account cannot write there.

title: Database is in emergency mode or damaged
message: Could not run BEGIN TRANSACTION in database 'X' because the database is in emergency mode or is damaged and must be restarted.
meaning: The tail of the buffer-pool cascade. By this point the database is not usable and the conversation is about recovery, not tuning.

title: Cannot open database requested by the login
message: Cannot open database "X" requested by the login. The login failed.
meaning: The login is fine. The database named in the connection string is missing, offline or not permitted.

title: Cannot open user default database
message: Cannot open user default database. Login failed.
meaning: The login's default database is unavailable. Fixable without touching the database.

title: ALTER TABLE cannot add that column to a non-empty table
message: ALTER TABLE only allows columns to be added that can contain nulls, or have a DEFAULT definition specified. Column 'X' cannot be added to non-empty table 'Y'.
meaning: Feels like 515 and is not. Adding a NOT NULL column with no default to a table that already has rows raises this instead.

title: Database could not be exclusively locked
message: The database could not be exclusively locked to perform the operation.
meaning: Something is connected. Common when setting a database to single user or restoring over it.

title: The filegroup cannot be removed because it is not empty
message: The filegroup 'X' cannot be removed because it is not empty.
meaning: Something still lives on it, often a nonclustered index rather than the table you were thinking of. Objects first, then the files, then the filegroup.

title: Operation not permitted in this database state
message: X is not permitted while a database is in the Y state.
meaning: The database is mid-transition, commonly RESTORING or RECOVERY_PENDING, and the statement you ran is not legal in that state. Read the state, not the statement.

title: Unable to open the physical file
message: Unable to open the physical file "X". Operating system error 5: "5(Access is denied.)".
meaning: Read the operating system error, not the SQL one. Error 5 has two different causes: the file is already open (often by SQL Server itself), or the service account cannot read it. On an attach it arrives with Msg 1802, and TRY/CATCH only sees the 1802.

title: CREATE FILE encountered operating system error
message: CREATE FILE encountered operating system error 5(Access is denied.) while attempting to open the file 'X'.
meaning: Service account permissions on the target folder, or a path that does not exist.

title: Not a primary database file
message: 'X.mdf' is not a primary database file.
meaning: A corrupt or wrong file being attached, or a file copied while the instance was running.

title: File header is not a valid database file header
message: The header for file 'X' is not a valid database file header. The Y property is incorrect.
meaning: Seen at startup against master: the file is there and SQL Server no longer recognises it as a database.

title: Files do not match the primary file of the database
message: One or more files do not match the primary file of the database.
meaning: Mismatched file set, usually an attach with the wrong files or a data file paired with the wrong log.

title: Ad hoc update to system catalogs is not supported
message: Ad hoc update to system catalogs is not supported.
meaning: RECONFIGURE refusing a configuration change that would write the catalogs directly. The setting, not the syntax, is the problem.

title: No permission to use KILL
message: User does not have permission to use the KILL statement.
meaning: KILL needs sysadmin, processadmin, or ALTER ANY CONNECTION. A login with none of the three gets this, tested on the lab.

title: Rollback status report cannot be obtained
message: Status report cannot be obtained. Rollback operation for Process ID X is not in progress.
meaning: KILL ... WITH STATUSONLY against a session that is not rolling back. Not an error about the session, an error about the question.

title: Arithmetic overflow converting to a data type
message: Arithmetic overflow error converting X to data type Y.
meaning: The intermediate value overflowed before the final one did. Applying a modulo or a cast earlier in the expression usually avoids it.

title: String or binary data would be truncated
message: String or binary data would be truncated.
meaning: Pre-2019 it will not tell you which column. 2019 and later name the column and the value.

title: Query processor ran out of internal resources
message: The query processor ran out of internal resources and could not produce a query plan.
meaning: Nearly always an enormous IN list or a generated query of extreme size.

title: Timeout waiting for memory resources
message: A timeout occurred while waiting for memory resources to execute the query.
meaning: RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE waits. Query memory grants are the thing to look at.

title: Page could not be processed
message: Object ID X, index ID Y, partition ID Z, alloc unit ID W (type ...): Page (1:368) could not be processed.  See other errors for details.
meaning: The summary line of a CHECKDB run, and it says so: read the other errors. One damaged page produces 8939, 8928, 8980 and 8978 together, which CHECKDB counts as four consistency errors on a single page rather than four faults.

title: Table error, an internal test failed on the page
message: Table error: Object ID X, index ID Y, partition ID Z, alloc unit ID W (type ...), page (1:368). Test (IS_OFF (BUF_IOERR, pBUF->bstat)) failed. Values are 133129 and -4.
meaning: An internal consistency test failed on the page itself. This is the one that describes the damage rather than its consequences.

title: Page is missing a reference from the previous page
message: Table error: Object ID X, index ID Y, partition ID Z, alloc unit ID W (type ...). Page (1:384) is missing a reference from previous page (1:368). Possible chain linkage problem.
meaning: The page chain is broken. Seen alongside 8939 and 8980 when a single page has gone; it describes the hole the damaged page left behind.

title: Index node refers to a child page that was not found
message: Table error: Object ID X, index ID Y, partition ID Z, alloc unit ID W (type ...). Index node page (1:376), slot 0 refers to child page (1:368) and previous child (0:0), but they were not encountered.
meaning: The index B-tree still points at the damaged page. Another view of the same fault, not a second one.

title: The log for the database is not available
message: The log for database 'X' is not available. Check the operating system error log for related error messages.
meaning: Severity 21, and it points you off the instance: the reason is normally in the OS error log, not in SQL Server.

title: Transaction log is full
message: The transaction log for database 'X' is full due to 'LOG_BACKUP'.
meaning: The reason in quotes is the diagnosis, and it is rarely solved by shrinking.

title: Existing connection was forcibly closed
message: A connection was successfully established with the server, but then an error occurred during the login process.
meaning: Not a login problem. The handshake failed before credentials were checked.

title: JSON text is not properly formatted
message: JSON text is not properly formatted. Unexpected character 'X' is found at position N.
meaning: Raised by the native JSON type and the JSON functions. The position in the message is exact; go to that character rather than re-reading the document.

title: User already exists in current database
message: User, group, or role 'X' already exists in the current database.
meaning: The classic orphaned user after a restore. The user exists, its SID no longer matches a login.

title: Database principal owns a schema
message: The database principal owns a schema in the database, and cannot be dropped.
meaning: Reassign the schema owner first, then drop the user.

title: Login owns one or more databases and cannot be dropped
message: Login 'X' owns one or more database(s). Change the owner of the database(s) before dropping the login.
meaning: Not a permission problem, an ownership one. Reassign the databases with ALTER AUTHORIZATION, then the drop succeeds.

title: The key is not encrypted using the specified decryptor
message: The key is not encrypted using the specified decryptor.
meaning: Severity 10, so it is informational rather than a failure. The key is real; the decryptor named is simply not one of the ones protecting it.

title: The current master key cannot be decrypted
message: The current master key cannot be decrypted. If this is a database master key, you should attempt to open it in the session before performing this operation.
meaning: FORCE will push the operation through and lose everything the old key protected, so establish why it cannot be decrypted before reaching for it.

title: An error occurred during decryption
message: An error occurred during decryption.
meaning: Almost always the wrong password. Reproduced by swapping the DECRYPTION BY PASSWORD and ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD values on a RESTORE MASTER KEY: this is the exact message it returns.

title: Cannot execute as the database principal
message: Cannot execute as the database principal because the principal "dbo" does not exist.
meaning: Usually a database whose owner SID no longer resolves, after a restore or a domain change.

title: Create or open the master key first
message: Please create a master key in the database or open the master key in the session before performing this operation.
meaning: The database master key exists but is not open in this session, or was never created. OPEN MASTER KEY first, or create one.

title: SSPI handshake failed
message: SSPI handshake failed with error code 0x8009030c.
meaning: Kerberos or NTLM could not complete. Usually a duplicate or missing SPN, or clock skew.

title: Login from an untrusted domain
message: Login failed. The login is from an untrusted domain and cannot be used with Integrated authentication.
meaning: Windows authentication could not be negotiated, often SPN or trust related rather than a password problem.

title: Login failed for user
message: Login failed for user 'X'.
meaning: The client only ever sees State 1. The real state is in the error log and names the cause.

title: Login disabled
message: Login failed for user 'X'. Reason: The account is disabled.
meaning: The login exists and the password may even be right. It is switched off.

title: Caller is not authorized to initiate the requested action
message: Caller is not authorized to initiate the requested action. X privileges are required.
meaning: A CDC administration refusal. The message names the privilege it wanted, which is the fastest read on it.

title: The event session has already been stopped
message: The event session has already been stopped.
meaning: ALTER EVENT SESSION ... STATE = STOP against a session that is not running. Harmless, but it prints a red error over an otherwise successful script, so guard the stop.

title: Cannot find server certificate
message: Cannot find server certificate with thumbprint 'X'.
meaning: A TDE-encrypted backup restored to an instance without the certificate. Restore the certificate first.

title: Certificate chain not trusted
message: The certificate chain was issued by an authority that is not trusted.
meaning: The client now validates the certificate by default. Your server did not change.
